The core operators define a dual-layered predictive architecture where presentation bias and relevance are modeled separately before being combined. Presentation bias models utilize positional and interface metadata to estimate inherent click tendencies, while relevancy models rely on IR metrics and query characteristics. These models operate under the assumption that user behavior can be decomposed into predictable components. Failure modes arise when these assumptions break down—such as during semantic drift or non-stationary user preferences—which necessitate adaptive retraining or dynamic adjustment mechanisms. Dualities emerge in how both models contribute to final ranking scores, with each serving as a kernel in a composite decision function. The system's robustness depends on maintaining independence between the two models' feature spaces to avoid redundancy and ensure complementary signal extraction.
